review_evidence_note: The official 2017/18 report documents active SnowPass sales and first-entry revenue in Engadin/South Grisons. It does not provide an explicit SnowPass operator roster on the cited pages, so Corviglia participation is not promoted to an exact historical fact.

The official 2023 report records CHF 656,000 of investment in digitalisation, infrastructure and vehicles, including a new piste machine, while winter cableway frequency fell 29 percent amid missing snow. These donor-specific changes overlap the post-anchor period.

The official 2022/23 graubündenCARD transport-benefits list names Bergbahnen Splügen-Tambo AG. The original 2023/24 file is indexed but returned HTTP 404 during reproducible collection, so exact continuity at the May 2023 anchor remains unresolved.

The official 2018/19 report documents SnowPass sales and revenue distribution across Grisons regions and companies. The cited pages do not explicitly enumerate participating operators, so Minschuns participation remains a qualified pass-environment risk rather than an exact fact.

The official 2017 report describes an independent family/leisure tourism business, a master-plan repositioning, and CHF 732,000 of investment, including CHF 500,000 for the valley-station expansion begun in October 2017. This directly overlaps the November 2017 treatment anchor.

The official 2018/19 report states that TopCard offered three freely chosen days in Upper Engadine, and the 2019/20 report documents the final SnowPass winter. This is direct evidence of competing-pass exposure around the anchor, though exact Corviglia operator terms still require the original tariff documents.

The official reports state that Samnaun-Ischgl left TopCard for winter 2018/19 and that SnowPass remained active through winter 2019/20. The donor is also a cross-border ski domain, so Austrian demand and policy shocks require separate review.
